excerpt: Our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) is our voluntary framework for managing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems.
paraphrase: The RSP is described as Anthropic's voluntary framework for managing catastrophic AI risks.

excerpt: It establishes how we identify and evaluate risks, how we make decisions about AI development and deployment, and, from the perspective of the world at large, how we aim to make sure that the benefits of our models exceed their costs.
paraphrase: The RSP sets out risk identification, deployment decision-making, and a societal cost-benefit aim.

excerpt: We have always intended for our RSP to be a living document.
paraphrase: Anthropic states the RSP has always been intended as a living document.

excerpt: We will continually update the RSP as we learn more about AI capabilities and risks, develop and refine technical safety measures, and gain more experience navigating an ecosystem in which the risks to society depend on the actions of many developers.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to continually updating the RSP as understanding, safety measures, and ecosystem experience evolve.

excerpt: The major components of this third iteration are as follows:
paraphrase: This introduces a list of the major components of the third iteration of the RSP.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety outline what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The recommendations describe what is needed industry-wide to keep catastrophic risks low during rapid AI advancement.

excerpt: We lay this out in a table that maps capability thresholds to the mitigations we believe they call for.
paraphrase: Anthropic presents a table mapping capability thresholds to corresponding mitigations.

excerpt: We also include our planned mitigations as a company, which are drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts.
paraphrase: The table also includes the company's own planned mitigations, sourced from elsewhere in the policy.

excerpt: This approach represents a change from our previous RSP, driven by a collective action problem.
paraphrase: The new approach reflects a change from the prior RSP due to a collective action problem.

excerpt: The overall level of catastrophic risk from AI depends on the actions of multiple AI developers, not just one.
paraphrase: Catastrophic AI risk depends on the collective actions of multiple developers, not one alone.

excerpt: Our previous RSP committed to implementing mitigations that would reduce our models' absolute risk levels to acceptable levels, without regard to whether other frontier AI developers would do the same.
paraphrase: The prior RSP committed to reducing absolute model risk levels regardless of other developers' actions.

excerpt: But from a societal perspective, what matters is the risk to the ecosystem as a whole.
paraphrase: From society's viewpoint, ecosystem-wide risk is what matters.

excerpt: If one AI developer paused development to implement safety measures while others moved forward with training and deploying AI systems without strong mitigations, that could result in a world that is less safe—the developers with the weakest protections would set the pace, and responsible developers would lose their ability to do safety research and advance the public benefit.
paraphrase: If a single developer pauses for safety while others proceed unmitigated, the weakest actors set the pace and responsible developers lose capacity to advance safety and public benefit.

excerpt: Although this situation has not yet arisen, it looks likely enough that we want to prepare for it.
paraphrase: This scenario hasn't occurred yet but seems likely enough to warrant preparation.

excerpt: We now separate our plans as a company—those which we expect to achieve regardless of what any other company does—from our more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
paraphrase: Anthropic now distinguishes its own achievable company plans from its broader industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: We aspire to advance the latter through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic aspires to advance industry-wide recommendations through example-setting, technical work, and advocacy.

excerpt: But we cannot commit to following them unilaterally.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot commit to unilaterally following the industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are a new requirement under our RSP.
paraphrase: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are introduced as a new RSP requirement.

excerpt: These will describe our concrete plans for making progress across Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.
paraphrase: The Roadmaps will lay out concrete plans across four domains: Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.

excerpt: Goals described in the Roadmaps are intended to be ambitious, yet achievable—providing the kind of forcing function that we consider to be a past success of our RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are meant to be ambitious yet achievable, serving as a forcing function similar to a prior RSP success.

excerpt: These are not hard commitments but rather public goals against which we will openly grade our progress.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are not binding commitments but public goals subject to open progress grading.

excerpt: Risk Reports are another new requirement.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are introduced as another new requirement.

excerpt: Risk Reports will provide detailed information on the safety profile of our models at the time of publication.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will detail the safety profile of models as of publication.

excerpt: They will go beyond describing model capabilities, addressing our thinking on how capabilities, threat models (the specific ways that models might pose threats), and active risk mitigations fit together, providing an assessment of the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will go beyond capabilities descriptions to explain how capabilities, threat models, and mitigations interrelate, with an overall risk assessment.

excerpt: These reports will reflect our reasoning as to whether we believe the risks of training or deploying our models are justified by their corresponding benefits to the world.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will explain whether training/deployment risks are justified by benefits.

excerpt: They will be published online, with some redactions to protect sensitive details about, for example, our training methods and organizations with whom we work.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published online with redactions to protect sensitive information such as training methods and partner organizations.

excerpt: As detailed below, we also aim to subject Risk Reports to review by credible, independent external parties.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to have Risk Reports reviewed by credible independent external parties.

excerpt: Finally, our governance commitments are intended to promote internal and external accountability, similar to those in our previous RSP.
paraphrase: Governance commitments aim to promote internal and external accountability, consistent with the prior RSP.

excerpt: Our RSP is only one part of our overall approach to safety.
paraphrase: The RSP is described as only one component of Anthropic's broader safety approach.

excerpt: For instance, although this policy focuses on catastrophic risks, they are not the only risks we consider important—our Usage Policy and societal impacts research address other concerns.
paraphrase: Other risks beyond catastrophic ones are addressed through the Usage Policy and societal impacts research.

excerpt: Further, the RSP may serve some regulatory requirements, but it is not designed to be comprehensive.
paraphrase: The RSP may partially serve regulatory requirements but is not intended to be comprehensive regulatory coverage.

excerpt: We want to keep it focused on our most central measures for addressing the catastrophic risks we prioritize most, rather than expand it to address every obligation we face.
paraphrase: Anthropic intends the RSP to remain focused on core catastrophic risk measures rather than covering every obligation.

excerpt: Where regulatory requirements exceed or differ from what the RSP covers, we will address them through separate documents.
paraphrase: Regulatory requirements beyond the RSP's scope will be handled in separate documents.

excerpt: "Catastrophic risk" as used in our RSP refers generally to risks of the most severe potential harms from advanced AI, such as existential threats or fundamental destabilization of global systems.
paraphrase: Footnote defining catastrophic risk generally as risks of the most severe potential harms including existential threats or global destabilization.

excerpt: We use this term in its plain meaning rather than adopting any specific statutory definition.
paraphrase: The term is used in its plain meaning, not tied to any specific statutory definition.

excerpt: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
paraphrase: Specific statutory thresholds, such as those in California SB 53, are addressed in separate compliance frameworks.

excerpt: This section outlines our recommendations for what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: This section describes recommendations for keeping catastrophic risk low industry-wide during rapid AI development.

excerpt: We lay this out in a three-column table.
paraphrase: The recommendations are presented in a three-column table.

excerpt: The left column identifies capability thresholds that would call for heightened mitigations.
paraphrase: The left column lists capability thresholds triggering heightened mitigations.

excerpt: The middle column provides an overview of our planned mitigations, which we have set forth more fully in our Frontier Safety Roadmap and other sections of this policy.
paraphrase: The middle column summarizes planned company mitigations detailed elsewhere in the policy and Roadmap.

excerpt: The right column describes our recommendations for industry-wide safety at each threshold.
paraphrase: The right column presents industry-wide safety recommendations for each threshold.

excerpt: The distinction between our plans as a company (middle column) and our industry-wide recommendations (right column) reflects the limitations of any single AI developer's ability to ensure safety across the industry.
paraphrase: The company-plan versus industry-recommendation distinction reflects that no single developer can ensure industry-wide safety alone.

excerpt: In particular, we cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to staying in line with the industry-wide recommendations in the right column.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unilaterally or unconditionally commit to the right-column industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
paraphrase: The recommendations will nonetheless shape important parts of Anthropic's work, as detailed below.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We use these recommendations as the north star for our risk mitigations planning as well as our public policy work.
paraphrase: The recommendations serve as the guiding standard for risk mitigation planning and public policy work.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We will strive to advance these recommendations through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will strive to advance the recommendations via example-setting, technical work, and advocacy.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We have also adopted a set of competitor-contingent commitments (see Appendix A) aimed at staying in line with these recommendations in scenarios where we can be confident that other relevant AI developers are doing the same.
paraphrase: Anthropic has adopted competitor-contingent commitments to follow the recommendations when confident that competitors do likewise, per Appendix A.

excerpt: At this point in AI's rapid development, we cannot presently give highly specific advance detail on what evaluations will determine whether risk thresholds have been passed, or what risk mitigations will be needed to achieve safety.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot currently specify in detail what evaluations will determine threshold crossing or what mitigations safety will require.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety are thus structured around requiring analysis and arguments making a strong case for safety, rather than AI Safety Levels (more in Appendix B).
paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendations rely on requiring safety-case analysis and argument rather than AI Safety Levels, elaborated in Appendix B.

excerpt: This leaves flexibility in how risk thresholds are evaluated and how safety is achieved and argued for.
paraphrase: This approach allows flexibility in evaluating thresholds and arguing for safety.

excerpt: But it creates a challenge: one actor's view of what constitutes good risk assessment and mitigation may be very different from another's.
paraphrase: This flexibility creates the challenge that risk-assessment standards may differ significantly between actors.

excerpt: Ultimately, the best way for these recommendations to be implemented is likely via governance of all relevant frontier AI developers by third parties that determine which developers need to provide risk analyses and make arguments for the safety of their systems, and determine which such arguments are adequate.
paraphrase: Anthropic believes third-party governance determining which developers must provide safety arguments, and judging adequacy, is the best implementation path.

excerpt: To the extent this takes the form of national regulation, different countries should attempt to harmonize their governance, including standards of evidence, to avoid a race to the bottom.
paraphrase: If implemented as national regulation, countries should harmonize governance and evidence standards to avoid a race to the bottom.

excerpt: In the shorter run, independent bodies (standards-setting organizations, auditors, etc.) might review such arguments and enforce high quality standards for private AI developers via voluntary mechanisms.
paraphrase: In the near term, independent bodies could review safety arguments and enforce standards voluntarily.

excerpt: We expect that the recommendations for industry-wide safety will evolve significantly, as we learn more about AI capabilities, threat models, and risk mitigations.
paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendations are expected to evolve significantly as understanding improves.

excerpt: We hope these recommendations will become increasingly specific over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes recommendations will grow more specific over time.

excerpt: Note that an AI developer might provide a single analysis covering a broad category of models, such that there isn't a new analysis needed for each release.
paraphrase: A single analysis may cover a broad model category rather than requiring per-release analysis.

excerpt: Additionally, determinations of which AI developers need to provide such analysis should be made with an effort to spare smaller AI developers from unnecessary compliance burden.
paraphrase: Determinations of which developers must provide analysis should try to spare smaller developers unnecessary compliance burden.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: AI systems with the ability to significantly help individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees) create/obtain and deploy chemical and/or biological weapons with serious potential for catastrophic damages.
paraphrase: The threshold is AI systems significantly enabling basic-background individuals or groups to create/deploy chemical or biological weapons with serious catastrophic potential.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We will maintain or improve on our ASL-3 protections, which include classifier guards at least as robust as our initial Constitutional Classifiers; access controls for trusted users with exemptions to classifier guards; red-teaming, bug bounties, and threat intelligence for continually assessing the threat of jailbreaks; and a number of noteworthy security controls.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain or improve ASL-3 protections including classifier guards, trusted-user access controls, red-teaming/bug bounties, threat intelligence, and security controls.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: Specifics may change, but we will maintain equally or more robust measures over time and will publish updates in our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Specific measures may change but robustness will be maintained or improved, with updates published in Risk Reports.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We expect to continuously meet the criteria in the right column, although we cannot make guarantees about an evolving landscape with continually adaptive attackers.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to continuously meet the right-column criteria but cannot guarantee this given adaptive attackers.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that individual users and relatively small teams will not become significantly more likely to cause catastrophic harm via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
paraphrase: Industry-wide recommendation: developers should argue that individuals/small teams are not significantly more likely to cause catastrophic harm via product use or weight theft.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. Lead-in: This will likely require:
excerpt: Restrictions on model behavior, and/or measures for quickly detecting and acting on Usage Policy violations, accompanied by a strong case that these measures are difficult to reliably, sustainably circumvent via jailbreaking.
paraphrase: Recommendation includes behavior restrictions or fast violation-detection paired with evidence these are hard to circumvent via jailbreaking.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. Lead-in: This will likely require:
excerpt: Precautions against opportunistic theft of model weights, such as centralized controls on third-party applications and software updates.
paraphrase: Recommendation includes precautions against opportunistic weight theft, such as centralized controls on third-party apps/updates.

excerpt: This column summarizes commitments drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts.
paraphrase: The middle column summarizes commitments described in more detail elsewhere.

excerpt: It should be read as an overview, not as indicating any separate or additional plans.
paraphrase: The column is an overview only, not a source of additional distinct commitments.

context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: AI systems that can functionally substitute for the scarce human expertise that is currently the primary barrier to novel development of chemical and biological weapons with potential for catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: The threshold covers AI systems that can substitute for the scarce human expertise currently limiting novel chem/bio weapon development with catastrophic potential.

context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: That is, a well-resourced team could, using the model, accomplish the end-to-end agent design and deployment (including, as relevant, agent design, verification and validation, formulation, and dissemination) that would otherwise require recruiting one of a small number of world-leading specialists.
paraphrase: A well-resourced team could use the model to accomplish end-to-end tasks that would otherwise require a rare world-leading specialist.

context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We will apply protections at least as strong as our ASL-3 protections (see previous row) to an expanded set of potential use cases for AI, covering the most likely vectors for this threat.
paraphrase: Anthropic will apply ASL-3-level or stronger protections to an expanded set of use cases covering the most likely threat vectors.

context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: Additionally, we will identify the most concerning specific threat pathways, create policy recommendations for early detection and response for such threats, and share this content with policymakers.
paraphrase: Anthropic will identify key threat pathways, develop early detection/response policy recommendations, and share these with policymakers.

context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that threat actors will not become significantly more likely to cause the sort of catastrophic harm discussed in the lefthand column via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
paraphrase: Industry-wide recommendation: developers should argue threat actors are not significantly more enabled to cause the described catastrophic harm via products or weight theft.

context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those from the previous row, but to a higher standard—to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
paraphrase: Similar measures apply but at a higher standard, such that even well-resourced threat actors would be unlikely to jailbreak or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized model access.

context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: This would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4, but it depends on the capabilities of the strongest and most plausible threat actors that are not bound by a credible governance regime enforcing the recommendations for industry-wide safety outlined here.
paraphrase: Security would likely need to match RAND SL4, though this depends on the capabilities of the strongest unregulated threat actors.

excerpt: In particular, weapons with the potential to cause events with consequences comparable to or worse than those of COVID-19.
paraphrase: The catastrophic harm threshold refers to consequences comparable to or worse than COVID-19.
stated_bar: consequences comparable to or worse than COVID-19

paraphrase: An example of a well-resourced team is one with millions of dollars and recent top-tier PhD support.

paraphrase: The focus is on realistically resourced teams matching real-world threat actors.

paraphrase: Example context: a world limited to the best AI models available as of 2023.

paraphrase: The threshold covers highly relied-upon AI systems with sensitive access and moderate autonomous/subterfuge capacity that could plausibly cause sabotage raising the odds of global catastrophe.

paraphrase: Near-term, this risk applies most to AI systems widely used internally at AI companies with the ability to manipulate successor-system training and safety evidence.

locator: Table / Misaligned AI systems / Capability threshold-c

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: AI systems that can fully automate, or otherwise dramatically accelerate, the work of large, top-tier teams of human researchers in domains where fast progress could cause threats to international security and/or rapid disruptions to the global balance of power—for example, energy, robotics, weapons development, and AI itself.
paraphrase: The threshold covers AI that can fully automate or dramatically accelerate top-tier research teams in domains threatening international security or global power balance.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: For now, our evaluations will focus specifically on AI R&D, as this domain likely plays to AI systems' current strengths and is more tractable to assess than capabilities in other domains.
paraphrase: Evaluations currently focus on AI R&D since it suits current AI strengths and is more tractable to assess.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: Additionally, AI R&D alone could cause acceleration in AI capabilities improvements, to the point where all of the threats listed above (and more) develop very quickly.
paraphrase: AI R&D automation alone could accelerate capabilities so much that all other listed threats develop rapidly.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: We will consider this threshold to be met if we determine that either (1) our models would be able to fully substitute for our entire set of Research Scientists and Research Engineers, at competitive costs (i.e., within a factor of 5); or (2) there is "dramatic acceleration" of the pace of AI progress for reasons that likely relate to the automation of AI R&D.
paraphrase: The threshold is met if models could fully substitute for all Research Scientists/Engineers at within 5x cost, or if dramatic AI-progress acceleration occurs due to AI R&D automation.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: We would consider scenario (2) to have occurred where (a) we observe or expect double the rate of progress in AI aggregate capabilities compared to both the rate we'd expect and the fastest rate of extended progress we've observed in the absence of significant AI contributions to AI R&D and (b) it is plausible that this doubling is substantially attributable to the automation of research and/or engineering.
paraphrase: Scenario 2 is met when observed/expected progress doubles relative to baseline expectations and historical rates without AI contribution, and this doubling is plausibly due to automation of research/engineering.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: (as opposed to other factors, such as increased headcount, compute, or general productivity), such that continuation of the trend in AI progress seems likely to lead to even greater acceleration.
paraphrase: The doubling must not be attributable to other factors like headcount or compute increases, and should suggest a trend toward even greater acceleration.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: This capability threshold is intended to reflect our definition of highly capable models (see Section 3.6).
paraphrase: This threshold reflects the definition of highly capable models detailed in Section 3.6.

excerpt: In particular, at this point AI systems might be responsible for much of the research and analysis that underpins risk assessment, and might have strong capabilities for deception, manipulation and obfuscation of evidence, in which case analyses of threats from AIs should follow very high evidentiary standards with thorough and careful analysis of the possibility that much of the key evidence is suspect due to the possibility of manipulation by AI systems.

paraphrase: The Roadmap will be shared with all full-time employees, the Board, and the LTBT, and published in redacted form.

paraphrase: Anthropic will report on goal achievement and set new goals upon achieving prior ones.

paraphrase: The Roadmap is subject to change.

paraphrase: Anthropic will try to avoid weakening goals merely due to inability to achieve them.

paraphrase: Anthropic will publish Risk Reports covering system risks and continuation determinations.

excerpt: These have significant content in common with system cards, but we are adding additional structure and process aimed at presenting our overall assessments of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports overlap with system cards but add structure and process for presenting overall risk assessments.

paraphrase: Each Risk Report covers risks as of a coverage date no more than 30 days before publication.

paraphrase: Coverage includes all publicly deployed models and internal models newly determined to pose significantly greater misalignment or automated R&D risk than previously covered models.

excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
paraphrase: At minimum, internal models deployed for large-scale fully autonomous research will be classified as in-scope.

excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as "in-scope models."
paraphrase: Qualifying models are termed in-scope models.

excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.
paraphrase: Additional models may voluntarily be included without expanding stated commitments.

paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published every 3-6 months.

excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Risk Reports differ from system cards in not being published per model release.

excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
paraphrase: Introductory statement to a list of guiding principles for Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
paraphrase: Anthropic intends Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers' AI models into account.
paraphrase: Anthropic will acknowledge significant absolute risk even where its marginal contribution to ecosystem risk is limited.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
paraphrase: Anthropic will invest significant effort in investigating and sharing risk findings.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place (or plan to implement shortly), we will keep our future practices in line with this description or track and report noteworthy changes and deviations (generally via subsequent Risk Reports).
paraphrase: Anthropic will either maintain consistency with described mitigations or report noteworthy deviations in later Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We should make a strong attempt to ensure that ongoing (as opposed to temporary) changes do not significantly increase the level of risk.
paraphrase: Anthropic should strongly attempt to prevent ongoing changes from significantly increasing risk.

excerpt: We will describe how we identify, evaluate, and mitigate catastrophic risks. A Risk Report will document the following:
paraphrase: Risk Reports will describe identification, evaluation, and mitigation of catastrophic risks, documenting listed items.

paraphrase: Risk Reports document the criteria for determining which catastrophic risks are assessed.

excerpt: Threat model specification: The relevant threat models (which will, at a minimum, include those discussed above).
paraphrase: Risk Reports specify the relevant threat models, including at minimum those already discussed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):

paraphrase: Risk Reports document capability/alignment evaluations and other evidence considered for each in-scope model.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):

paraphrase: Risk Reports document mitigations implemented per in-scope model across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment, with effectiveness discussion.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):

paraphrase: Risk Reports include any other considerations material to the risk analysis.

excerpt: We will provide our reasoning and conclusions regarding both specific threat models and overall risk levels. Our analyses will include:
paraphrase: Risk analyses will provide reasoning and conclusions on threat models and overall risk levels.

paraphrase: For each threat model, the remaining absolute risk after mitigations will be analyzed.

excerpt: We will also discuss whether we believe we've crossed relevant thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1), and (as relevant) whether we believe we're meeting the risk mitigation standards corresponding to them.
paraphrase: The report will discuss whether industry-wide safety thresholds have been crossed and whether corresponding mitigation standards are met.

excerpt: Overall risk assessment: We will provide an overall risk assessment.
paraphrase: The report will provide an overall risk assessment.

excerpt: Risk-benefit determination: We will explain whether, and if so why, we believe the identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.
paraphrase: The report will explain whether identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.

excerpt: Looking forward: We will outline our plans for continuing to monitor and mitigate the relevant risks over time.
paraphrase: The report will outline plans for ongoing monitoring and mitigation.

excerpt: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
paraphrase: Introductory lead-in to items addressed under review of past Risk Reports and decisions.

paraphrase: The report addresses noteworthy deviations or changes in risk mitigation practices since the previous report and their risk implications.

paraphrase: The report addresses internal deployment decisions on in-scope models that occurred between Risk Reports.

paraphrase: The report addresses changes to the Frontier Safety Roadmap and any missed goals.

paraphrase: The report will explain how competitive comparisons influenced the risk assessment.

paraphrase: All above assessments will be conducted for each in-scope model.

paraphrase: Similar models may be analyzed together with justification to avoid redundancy.

paraphrase: Internal subject matter experts conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.

paraphrase: Comprehensive internal feedback will be solicited to identify weaknesses, gaps, or needed clarifications.

paraphrase: Feedback may be used to refine the report, and external expert feedback will usually also be sought.

paraphrase: The Risk Report and feedback will be sent to the CEO and RSO for final review and approval.

paraphrase: The CEO and RSO make the final determination on adequacy of the risk assessment and downstream plans.

paraphrase: After approval, the CEO and RSO promptly share the decision, report, and feedback with the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: By "marginal risk analysis," we mean arguing that the risks imposed by our systems in particular are relatively lower when keeping in mind the risks unavoidably posed by other AI systems.

paraphrase: When marginal risk analysis is a major factor in a decision, the Board and LTBT must explicitly approve the Risk Report instead of just the CEO and RSO.

paraphrase: A public version of the Risk Report will be published.

paraphrase: Anthropic aims to minimize redactions in both the public version and the version shared with regular-clearance employees.

paraphrase: Redactions may be made to comply with legal obligations such as export controls or contractual duties.

paraphrase: Redactions may protect proprietary technical and business information.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Privacy: To protect the personal privacy of individuals.
paraphrase: Redactions may protect individuals' personal privacy.

paraphrase: Anthropic will disclose that redactions occurred and aim to briefly justify them, though justifications may be high-level.

excerpt: We will work toward a practice of seeking comprehensive, public external review on our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Anthropic will work toward comprehensive public external review of Risk Reports.

excerpt: This means working with one or more third-party organizations that will receive private versions of our Risk Reports (unredacted or with minimal redactions, as discussed below) and publish comprehensive commentary on them.
paraphrase: External review involves third-party organizations receiving mostly unredacted reports and publishing comprehensive commentary.

excerpt: Commentary will address topics including the quality of our reasoning, the validity of our risk assessments, the overall level of risk, and whether the redactions we've made for the public version are reasonable and appropriate.
paraphrase: External commentary will cover reasoning quality, risk assessment validity, overall risk level, and reasonableness of redactions.

excerpt: Our intent is for external reviewers' judgments to carry significant weight in the eyes of the public as well as our employees.
paraphrase: Anthropic intends for external reviewers' judgments to carry significant public and internal weight.

excerpt: But there are no well-established organizations or procedures for this sort of practice, and we are approaching it as an experiment.
paraphrase: No well-established organizations or procedures exist yet, so this is being approached experimentally.

paraphrase: A full external review with at least one reviewer is required whenever a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted.

context_stem: Definitions for full external review trigger:

paraphrase: A model is deemed highly capable if it crosses the automated AI R&D threshold defined in Section 1.

context_stem: Definitions for full external review trigger:

paraphrase: Significantly redacted means omissions that would prevent a reader from meaningfully evaluating the conclusions using only the public version.

excerpt: A report shall be deemed significantly redacted if, in the judgment of the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT, it meets this description.
paraphrase: The RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT can judge a report to be significantly redacted.

excerpt: Note that unredacted reports will be shared with a large number of employees, who will be in a position to raise concerns if they believe the public version meets this description.
paraphrase: Unredacted reports shared broadly with employees allow them to raise concerns about redaction adequacy.

paraphrase: Upon LTBT request, a public or private external review of the Risk Report will be conducted.

excerpt: We will select external reviewers that:
paraphrase: Lead-in to criteria for selecting external reviewers.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:

paraphrase: Reviewers must have significant expertise evaluating dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.

paraphrase: Reviewers should understand ways evaluations could be misleading, such as alignment faking.

paraphrase: Reviewers should have incentives favoring candor over pleasing Anthropic.

paraphrase: Reviewers should not be entirely financially or reputationally dependent on Anthropic and similar companies.

paraphrase: Individuals conducting the review and their superiors must lack financial interest in or close personal relationships with anyone at Anthropic.

excerpt: In selecting external reviewers, we will consult with the Board and obtain the approval of the LTBT.
paraphrase: External reviewer selection involves Board consultation and LTBT approval.

excerpt: The external review process will involve sharing the Risk Report with one or more external reviewers within one week of submitting the same report to our Board and LTBT.
paraphrase: The Risk Report will be shared with external reviewers within one week of submission to the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: We will ask the external reviewers to provide public commentary on our report within 30 days of receipt.
paraphrase: External reviewers will be asked to provide public commentary within 30 days of receiving the report.

excerpt: We will try to work toward a process that involves the full external review being completed prior to Board/LTBT review (and may require this later).
paraphrase: Anthropic will work toward completing full external review before Board/LTBT review, potentially making this mandatory later.

excerpt: All sections of the Risk Report will be shared with at least one external reviewer, but we may choose to split the review process across different external reviewers based on their subject matter expertise.
paraphrase: All sections will be shared with at least one reviewer, potentially split across multiple reviewers by expertise.

excerpt: For purposes of external review, the only redactions to the Risk Report will be those necessary to comply with legal prohibitions or to maintain our legal rights.
paraphrase: For external review purposes, redactions are limited to those legally necessary.

excerpt: We expect that we will also invest some time in answering follow-up questions from parties doing external review.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to spend time answering follow-up questions from external reviewers.

excerpt: For example, we may redact information if sharing it would endanger our legal right to treat it as confidential. This would be an uncommon situation.
paraphrase: Redaction may occur to preserve confidentiality rights, though this is expected to be uncommon.

paraphrase: Sensitivity alone or leak-risk reduction is not a basis for redaction.

paraphrase: The review assesses whether the report contains sufficient information about identified risks.
